help.introDesc: A mod management tool designed for Nintendo Switch. Built on a brand new architecture with a complete rewrite and expanded features. This project is open-source and permanently free, with no paid content of any kind. Due to limited personal development capacity, the collection and maintenance of online mod resources depends on community participation and contributions.
help.introHighlightsDesc:
· Modern and clean UI design
· Deep Chinese language support
· Simple and intuitive workflow
· Supports both ZIP and folder mod formats
· Automatically converts pchtxt patches to IPS patches
· Smart detection of non-standard mod structures
· Strict multi-mod file conflict handling
· One-click disable or restore all mods
· Quickly add games from installed game list
· Add mods via FTP and MTP
· Built-in online mod store
· Fast and efficient search
· Rich mod customization options
· Light and dark themes with system-following option
· In-app update check and download
help.disclaimerSoftwareDesc: This project is maintained by one person who is not a professional developer. There is no guarantee that the software is free of critical bugs. Any save data corruption or mod file damage that may result is the user's own responsibility.
help.disclaimerServiceDesc: The server and website are also maintained by the author alone, purely out of passion, with no guarantee of long-term operation. However, this project will always remain free. If maintenance becomes impossible, the server and data will be handed over to someone willing to continue.
help.disclaimerCopyrightDesc: If any user-uploaded mod infringes on the original author's rights, please contact me and it will be removed immediately.
help.donateStatementDesc: Thank you to every user. Using this project is itself a form of support. The project will always remain free and open-source, with no paid privileges. However, as the number of users grows, the cost of keeping the servers running and maintaining the project has exceeded initial expectations. Long-term stable operation now faces considerable pressure. If you would like to further support the project with a donation, please scan one of the QR codes below.
help.feedbackInfoDesc: When submitting bug reports, please use GitHub Issues as the preferred channel, and provide complete and accurate information. Due to limited personal capacity, reports that are incomplete or vaguely described will not be actively followed up with repeated clarification requests. Thank you for your understanding.
help.feedbackRequireDesc:
· Atmosphere and system firmware version
· Detailed steps that trigger the issue
· Whether the issue is consistently reproducible
· If only triggered by a specific file, please provide it
· Any other information helpful for diagnosing the issue
help.guideIntroDesc: Below is a basic usage overview. For more detailed tutorials with screenshots and videos, scan the QR codes at the bottom.
help.guideAddGameDesc: On the home page, press  to add from the online mod store, or press  to go to the local add page and add local mods to a game via MTP or FTP.
help.guideTransferDesc: Local adding supports both ZIP and folder mod formats. Use the MTP or FTP option in the menu to transfer mod files to the transit area. After transfer, tap the target game card and select mods from the transit area to add.
help.guideInstallDesc: In the mod list, tap a mod card to install or uninstall it. File conflicts between mods are automatically detected during installation.
help.faqModFormat: What are ZIP type and folder type mods
help.faqModFormatDesc:
The software supports two mod types. The built-in smart recognition algorithm can automatically parse mod directory structures, so files do not need to follow a strict standard layout.
· ZIP type: mod files packaged as a ZIP archive, the archive name is used as the mod name
· Folder type: mod files stored directly as a directory, the top-level folder name is used as the mod name
· Note: All file names must use English characters only. Non-English characters will cause operations to fail.
help.faqTransfer: How to transfer mod files to the console
help.faqTransferDesc: The software supports two transfer methods, accessible from the menu on the Add Game or Mod List pages via . MTP requires a USB cable connection to your computer — a storage device named "Add Mod" will appear on your PC, simply drag files into it. FTP requires the console and computer to be on the same Wi-Fi network — the app will display an FTP address to connect with an FTP client. ZIP files are recommended for MTP high-speed transfer, while folder-based mods work best with FTP using multi-threaded mode. Transferred files are stored in the transit area, awaiting assignment to a game.
help.faqUpload: How to upload mods to the store
help.faqUploadDesc: Mod uploads must be done via the web. Press  on the home page to open the store menu, select "View Website" and scan the QR code to access the web store. The web interface provides mod browsing and uploading. When uploading, select the corresponding game and fill in basic mod information. Uploaded mods will appear in the online store after review. Please obtain the original author's permission before uploading. Uploading paid, pornographic, or sensitive content is strictly prohibited and will result in a permanent ban.
help.faqTransitEmptyDesc: The transit area is a temporary storage location for mod files, located at /mods2/!temp_mods/ on the SD card. Files transferred via MTP or FTP are stored here first. This message means no mod files are in transit. Please upload mods via MTP or FTP from the menu first, then tap a game card to select and add mods.
help.faqNetworkDesc: Store browsing, mod downloads, and online game name retrieval all require a network connection. If you see network-related errors, verify that your console is connected to Wi-Fi. If the network is fine but access still fails, the server may be temporarily unavailable. Also ensure your Switch has been time-synced, as incorrect time can cause network request failures.
help.faqInvalidModDesc: This message means no valid mod file structure was found in the folder or ZIP archive. A valid mod must contain at least one of: romfs, romfslite, exefs, cheats, exefs_patches, romfs.bin, or a pchtxt patch file.
help.faqConflictDesc: When installing a mod, the software checks if any files it modifies are already occupied by other mods. If two mods modify the same file with different content, a conflict is detected and the conflicting mod name is shown. You need to uninstall the conflicting mod first. Files with identical content across multiple mods do not trigger conflicts — the software uses reference counting to manage shared files safely.
help.faqRemoveGame: Cannot remove game with installed mods
help.faqRemoveGameDesc: To prevent installed mod files from being left behind in system directories, all mods must be uninstalled before removing a game. Go to the game's mod list, uninstall each installed mod, then remove the game. After removal, mod files are automatically moved to the transit area for future use.
help.faqDuplicateTidDesc: TID is a unique identifier for each game. The software uses TID to manage mod files. If the same TID exists in different SD card directories, it causes data management conflicts. Duplicate games are highlighted in red on the home page. Please manually merge folders with the same TID into one, ensuring each TID maps to a single directory.
help.faqForceCleanDesc: Force clean repairs reference count file corruption caused by abnormal interruptions (e.g., sleep, forced shutdown) during mod installation or uninstallation. Corrupted reference counts can cause conflict detection errors or incomplete uninstalls. After force cleaning, all installed mod files in the game directory are deleted (including manually installed mods), and mods need to be reinstalled. This operation cannot be undone — use it only when the above issues are confirmed.
help.faqCustomDesc: Due to Switch input limitations, editing mod names, descriptions, and version numbers on the console is indeed inconvenient. However, these customization features are optional extensions — they do not affect core operations like installing and uninstalling mods. If you find it cumbersome, feel free to use only the core features. But please do not use this as grounds for thoughtless criticism, or you will likely receive a sarcastic response from the author.

modList.firstLaunchBasicBody: This page is for managing mods for the current game. Select a mod and press  to install or uninstall it. Do not leave this page during installation or uninstallation to avoid data corruption. If an issue occurs, use "Force Clean" from the menu to repair it.
modList.firstLaunchShortcutsBody:
- Press  to quickly open the mod store for the current game.
- Press  to view the store details of the selected mod.
- Press  to open the menu and view more management options.
modList.firstLaunchLocalAddBody: First, use MTP or FTP from the menu to transfer mod files to the transit area. Then select the mods you want to add under "Local Add". Please refer to the menu descriptions for MTP and FTP precautions.
modList.firstLaunchNoticeBody: All files and directories must use English-only names. Using non-English characters will cause the operation to fail and leave residual files.
modList.mhriseFirstLaunchTitle: Monster Hunter Rise: All Versions Supported!
modList.mhriseFirstLaunchBody: Because this game's mod management rules are very complex, install and uninstall mods only through this manager. Using a third-party manager, or manually adding or modifying Monster Hunter Rise mod files on the SD card, will inevitably cause installation or uninstallation errors.
modList.mhriseFirstLaunchTroubleshootingBody: If mod issues occur, use "Force Clean" from the menu to quickly delete all Monster Hunter Rise mod files from the SD card, then reinstall the mods you need.
modList.dontStarveFirstLaunchTitle: Don't Starve (Single Player) Is Now Fully Supported!
modList.dontStarveFirstLaunchBody: This game's management rules are complex, and although the manager supports manually added mods, it cannot synchronize records of those operations, causing its management state to differ from the actual files on the SD card. Therefore, use this manager consistently for installation and uninstallation rather than mixing it with third-party managers or manual changes.
modList.dontStarveFirstLaunchUsageBody: Mods for this game require a prerequisite framework, which can be downloaded and installed from the Mod Store. Once the framework is installed, all other mods can be installed or uninstalled directly through this manager; required special directories and numbering are handled automatically.
modList.dontStarveFirstLaunchTroubleshootingBody: If mod issues occur, use "Force Clean" from the menu to quickly delete all Don't Starve mod files from the SD card, then reinstall the mods you need.
modList.unmanagedDetectedBody: Mods for this game that are not yet managed by this manager were detected on the SD card. To prevent installation status conflicts and leftover files, these mods must first be extracted into the manager before you can continue managing this game.
modList.unmanagedExtractionBody: Extraction only moves the relevant files from the system mod directory into the manager. Cheats and other mod files will be saved separately. Extracted mods are left uninstalled by default, and you can reinstall them.
modList.unmanagedNoticeBody: Do not exit the application or power off the console during extraction. Selecting "Back" returns to the Home page, selecting "Confirm" starts extraction immediately.
modList.forceCleanDesc:
Used to fix corrupted counter files caused by abnormal interruption during mod install or uninstall.
 - This will force uninstall all mods for this game, including manually installed mods on SD card. Use with caution.
 - Corrupted counter files may cause conflict detection errors and incomplete mod uninstallation.
